overview: Adds POST /api/notifications/send — a single-step, synchronous FCM dispatch endpoint. The caller provides only title and body; the platform resolves the FCM token internally, dispatches immediately, and persists an audit record with status=dispatched. No change to the existing scheduler path.

in_scope: Schema migration: make label and deep_link nullable; allow fire_at to be NULL (NULL = immediate send)
Internal FCM token resolution from notifications.device WHERE device_id='default'
Synchronous FCM dispatch in the request handler (not via scheduler)
out_of_scope: Scheduling path (fire_at, APScheduler, dispatch job) — unchanged

persistence.migration_description: ALTER TABLE notifications.notification: make label nullable with DEFAULT '', make deep_link nullable with DEFAULT '', make fire_at nullable (NULL represents immediate-send, non-NULL represents scheduled). Existing rows are unaffected. The dispatch job already filters WHERE status='pending' AND fire_at <= NOW(); NULL fire_at rows will never match (NULL comparisons return NULL/false), so immediate-send rows are invisible to the scheduler.

error_cases.condition: No row in notifications.device WHERE device_id='default'
error_cases.message: No default device registered. Open AtlasPhone to register an FCM token.

error_cases.condition: FCM dispatch call raises an exception
error_cases.message: FCM dispatch failed. The notification was not delivered.

ImmediateSendRequest.title: str — required, non-empty, Android notification title
ImmediateSendRequest.body: str — required, non-empty, Android notification body text
ImmediateSendRequest.source: str — optional, defaults to 'claude', stored for audit only

ImmediateSendResponse.id: str — UUID of the persisted notification record
ImmediateSendResponse.title: str — echoed from request
ImmediateSendResponse.dispatched_at: datetime (ISO-8601 UTC) — server time at the moment FCM send() returned successfully

POST /api/notifications/send: 1. Validate request body against ImmediateSendRequest (title required, body required, source defaults to 'claude')
2. Query notifications.device WHERE device_id='default'; if no row → return 503 NO_DEFAULT_DEVICE
5. Call send_fcm_message(token=fcm_token, notification_id=..., title=..., body=..., label='', deep_link='') — synchronous; if raises → return 502 FCM_DISPATCH_FAILED (no DB write on FCM failure)

6. INSERT INTO notifications.notification (id, source, fire_at, title, body, label, deep_link, fcm_token, status) VALUES (..., NULL, ..., '', '', <fcm_token>, 'dispatched') RETURNING id, title, body, dispatched_at (NOTE: dispatched_at is not a column — use created_at as the audit timestamp; the response dispatched_at is the value captured in step 4 and passed to the INSERT as created_at override or returned from application logic)
internal_flow.time_authority: Server time (datetime.now(timezone.utc)) captured after successful FCM send() call. This is the authoritative dispatched_at value.

schema_notes.dispatched_at_column: The existing notifications.notification table does not have a dispatched_at column. The response field dispatched_at is derived from server time captured in application logic (step 4 above), not read back from the database. The persisted record uses created_at (auto-set by DEFAULT NOW()) as the audit timestamp. The response dispatched_at is the in-memory datetime from step 4.
schema_notes.fire_at_null_semantics: NULL fire_at means immediate send. The dispatch job WHERE fire_at <= NOW() never matches NULL rows (SQL NULL comparison = NULL, not true). No scheduler change needed.
schema_notes.label_deep_link_empty_string: Immediate-send rows store label='' and deep_link='' (empty string, not NULL). These are passed to send_fcm_message as data fields per the FCM payload contract v1.0. The Android app receives them as empty strings. No Android change required.

contracts.fcm_token_never_logged: INVARIANT: fcm_token fetched from notifications.device is used only for FCM dispatch. It must not appear in any log output (matches existing module invariant).
contracts.fcm_token_never_in_response: INVARIANT: fcm_token must never appear in ImmediateSendResponse or any HTTP response body.
contracts.no_db_write_on_fcm_failure: If FCM dispatch raises, no notification record is written to Postgres. The 502 response is the only artifact of a failed dispatch.
contracts.idempotency: POST /api/notifications/send is not idempotent. Each call produces a new UUID and a new FCM dispatch.
contracts.existing_scheduler_path_unchanged: The APScheduler dispatch job, POST /api/notifications/, DELETE /api/notifications/{id}, and POST /api/notifications/{id}/replace are entirely unchanged.
contracts.single_device: This endpoint always targets device_id='default'. Multi-device support is out of scope.

external: firebase_admin (already initialised on startup via init_fcm())
